correctness.rationale: Lemma 1 proves each feasible signature corresponds to a coset of the binary cycle space, size 2^c. For cacti, the c edge-disjoint cycles form a cycle basis, and whole-cycle reversals preserve coherent directed-cycle status. Conversely, directing three internally disjoint theta paths from one endpoint to the other and reversing the union of two paths gives acyclic versus cyclic orientations with identical indegree parities. The orientation count factors over bridges and cycles; division by 2^c is legitimate because every signature fibre has constant directed-cycle count. The checker verifies all 772 connected labeled graphs on up to five vertices for the iff condition and checks exact polynomials on individual and multi-cycle cacti. Neither these checks nor the search is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Motivated by the 2026 parity-constrained acyclic orientation existence problem, the result gives an exact structural iff characterization across all connected simple graphs of when indegree parity makes acyclicity invariant and identifies theta as an obstruction. On the maximal class it enumerates every feasible signature by the number of forced directed cycles and in particular counts successful targets exactly for arbitrarily many cactus cycles. These are substantive global structure and exact enumeration, not merely rephrasing rank or a small finite case.
